metadata.title: Midjourney, Part One.
metadata.audience: HAI Lyrical Literacy volunteers opening Midjourney for the first time. Internal training, not promotion.
metadata.narration_notes: Host is Rohan V. Full name spoken EXACTLY ONCE, in BOUT. Phonetic spellings are deliberate for Kokoro G2P: 'Rohaan' = Row-Haan. Do NOT 'correct' them. Register is internal volunteer training - never promotional. Access is stated ONCE, in B02, as a mechanical route; no pricing, no plan names, no selling. The VIDEO COUNT IS NEVER STATED - Suno Part 1 said 'the first of three' and that forced a cramped Part 3; this says 'this series'. NO VERSION NUMBER anywhere: the settings panel is not in this part, and the 'Help us improve V8' row is omitted from every mockup. Every MjL1* scene passes kicker='LYRICAL LITERACY - MIDJOURNEY TUTORIAL PART 1'. Heteronym pass done: 'record' rewritten to 'ran with' (B06), 'lives' rewritten to 'sits' (B07), 'separate' rewritten to 'independent' (B05), 'read' rewritten to 'look at' (BVDT). UI ground truth is MIDJOURNEY-UI-SPEC.md, built from 23 first-hand captures.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Rohaan from Humanitarians AI. This is the first video in our Midjourney series. Midjourney turns a written description into images. This one covers getting in, finding your way around, and making your first set of images. Everything before you start tuning anything.

show.event: Composer fades up; serif greeting 'Hi, HAI' above it
The ask types itself into the composer
Send arms terracotta; running indicator appears
Three result lines reveal - what this video covers

props.command: I have never opened Midjourney. Where do I start?
output: Signing in, and whose account you land in.
The eight things down the left, and the bar across the top.
Your first images - and what the feed records about them.

beats.act: Act 1 - executive summary (BLUF): the whole tool is one loop
beats.narration_text: The whole tool is one loop. You type a description into a single box at the top. Midjourney hands back four images. You pick one and take it further. Everything else, the settings, the references, the editor, is a way of steering that loop. Learn the loop first and the rest has somewhere to attach.

show.event: Three stage cards outline, dimmed, spanning the content rect
Stage 1 lights; a prompt types itself into a Midjourney-style box
Stage 2 lights; four tiles resolve one after another - a ROW, not a quad
Stage 3 lights; one tile is ringed and an action stack appears beside it
Closing line: settings, references and the editor all steer this loop

props.sparkLine: One box. Four images. Pick one.

beats.act: Act 2 - access, and whose account you land in
beats.narration_text: Access runs through Discord. Join the Humanitarians AI server first, then open midjourney dot com and choose the Discord option when it asks how you want to sign in. Same route as Suno. One thing worth knowing: you land in the shared Humanitarians AI account, not a personal one. Everything you generate sits in the same library the rest of the team can see.

show.event: Two step cards and a note card outline, dimmed
Step 1 lights: the HAI Discord chip
Step 2 lights: a 'Continue with Discord' control, with 'not email, not Google' beside it
The note lights: the captured sidebar account chip, and what a shared account means

beats.act: Act 3 - the sidebar: eight items, three groups
beats.narration_text: Eight items run down the left, in three groups. Four sit on their own: Explore, Create, Edit, Organize. Three sit under Aesthetics: Personalize, Moodboards, Style Creator. One sits under Community: Tasks. For today only two of them matter. Create is where you work. Organize is where everything you have made ends up.

show.event: The app window enters; its sidebar carries an accent outline
The annotation rail enters with the count card
Group 1 lights: Explore, Create, Edit, Organize
Group 2 lights: Personalize, Moodboards, Style Creator; then Community
The landing card lights: Create is where you work, Organize is where it ends up

beats.act: Act 4 - the imagine bar and the header cluster
beats.narration_text: The bar across the top is the whole input. You type in the middle. The picture icon on the left attaches an image to your prompt. The sliders icon on the right opens the settings. Beside the bar sits a P, which is personalization, and a search box whose label changes with the page. Three of those are later parts. Today you only need the middle.

show.event: A locator strip shows where the bar sits in the window; the bar is ringed
The bar and cluster enter at reading size; four note cards outline beneath
The text field rings
The add-image icon rings
The sliders icon rings
The header cluster rings; the search label cycles through its captured variants

props.sparkLine: One bar. Four things on it.

beats.act: Act 5 - submitting, and the three progress states
beats.narration_text: Press enter and four tiles appear as flat grey boxes, the first one marked Starting. A moment later they fill with blurred colour and a percentage counting up. Then they sharpen into four finished images. That is one job producing four results at once, not four independent attempts. All four came from the same prompt.

show.event: The prompt types into the imagine bar
Four flat grey tiles appear; the first carries a 'Starting…' chip
Tiles fill with blurred colour; the chip becomes a counting percentage
Tiles sharpen left to right; the chip goes away and an 'ar 1:1' chip appears on the rail
The line lands: one job, four results, not four attempts

beats.act: Act 6 - the rail beside your row: prompt, references, chips
beats.narration_text: To the right of every row sits the prompt, in full. If you attached reference images, their thumbnails sit underneath it. Then a line of small grey chips showing what that job ran with, an aspect ratio, or a stylize and weirdness value. So the feed is not just a wall of pictures. Every row keeps its own recipe, and you never have to remember how you got something.

show.event: The window enters showing TWO feed rows, so the chips can be seen to differ
The prompt text rings on row one
The reference thumbnails ring
The 'stylize 150' and 'weird 4' chips ring; row two brightens showing a bare 'ar 3:2'
The line lands: you never have to remember how you got something

props.sparkLine: Every row carries its own recipe.

beats.act: Act 7 - hover actions, and where Upscale is not
beats.narration_text: Hover over a finished image and three buttons appear along the bottom: Vary Subtle, Vary Strong, and Animate. Vary gives you a fresh set of four, a small step from this image or a large one. Animate turns the still into a short video. A trash icon and a heart sit in the top corners. Notice there is no Upscale here. That one sits in the panel you get when you open an image.

show.event: A single tile enters at reading size; the rest of its row sits beneath, dimmed
The hover overlay arrives as one thing: trash, heart and the three buttons together
The Vary card lights
The Animate card lights
The corners card lights, then the dashed card noting Upscale is in Part 2

beats.narration_text: To review. Sign in through Discord. Type a description in the bar at the top. Wait through the three states, grey, blurred, then sharp. Look at the chips beside your row to see what the job actually ran with. Then hover to vary or animate. That is the loop, end to end.

show.event: Artifact card fades up on the cream page
Lines reveal one at a time as the narration reaches them

artifactLines: Sign in - join the HAI Discord, then choose Discord at midjourney.com.
You land in the shared Humanitarians AI account, not a personal one.
Sidebar - 8 items: 4 on their own, 3 under Aesthetics, 1 under Community.
The bar - type in the middle; image icon attaches, sliders icon opens settings.
Submit - grey tiles, then blurred with a counter, then four sharp images.
One job returns four results. Not four attempts.
The rail beside each row keeps the prompt, any references, and the chips.
Hover - Vary Subtle, Vary Strong, Animate. Upscale is not on hover.

beats.narration_text: That is enough to make images today. Part 2 is about what goes in the box. Midjourney publishes a list of seven things a prompt should answer, and we work through it against a real prompt from this workspace. Try a few before then.

show.event: Composer returns with the Part 2 question
Three result lines reveal - what Part 2 covers

props.command: What do we cover in Midjourney Part 2?
output: Seven things a prompt should answer - Midjourney's own list.
A real prompt from this workspace, checked against all seven.
And what to write instead of 'no' in your prompt.
